# 2 Maccabees Chapter 1 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 2 Maccabees 1 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/2MA_001_page_001.jpg

---

**1** From the Jewish community in Jerusalem and Judea, along with our council of elders and Judas Maccabeus — to our fellow Jews in Egypt: we send you greetings and wish you lasting peace.

**2** May God bless you richly, and may he keep faith with the covenant he made with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, his servants who trusted him completely.

**3** May he give each of you a heart devoted to worshiping him and to fulfilling his will eagerly and wholeheartedly.

**4** May he open your minds to his law and his commandments, and may he grant you peace and security.

**5** May he hear you when you pray, may he be at peace with you, and may he never abandon you when times are hard.

**6** Even now we are here praying on your behalf.

**7** Back in the reign of Demetrius, in the year 169, we wrote to you about the desperate crisis that overtook us in those years — from the time when Jason and his faction betrayed the holy land and abandoned the kingdom,

**8** burning the temple gate and shedding the blood of the innocent. We cried out to the LORD and were heard. We offered sacrifice and grain offerings, we lit the sacred lamps, and we set out the bread of the Presence.

**9** Now we urge you: keep the festival of the twenty-fifth of Chislev — what we celebrate as the Feast of Booths in winter.

**10** In the year 188 — from the people of Jerusalem and Judea, from our council of elders and from Judas — to Aristobulus, adviser to King Ptolemy and himself a descendant of the anointed priestly line, and to all our Jewish brothers in Egypt: greetings and health.

**11** God has rescued us from terrible dangers, and for that we are deeply grateful — all the more since we were facing a king of such power.

**12** It was he who drove back the forces that had assembled against the holy city.

**13** When Antiochus marched into Persia at the head of an army that everyone thought was unstoppable, the priests of Nanea lured him into a trap and cut him down inside the temple.

**14** Antiochus had come under the pretense of marriage, bringing his officers with him — really just looking to make off with the enormous so-called dowry of the temple treasury.

**15** The priests of Nanea set the money out as bait, and when Antiochus entered the inner sanctuary with only a small escort, they locked the doors behind him.

**16** Then they slid open a hidden panel in the ceiling and rained stones down on the men below. They hacked the bodies to pieces and tossed the heads out to the crowd waiting outside.

**17** Blessed be our God in every way — he is the one who handed those godless men over to their fate!

**18** Since we will be celebrating the purification of the temple on the twenty-fifth day of Chislev, we wanted to make sure you knew about it, so that you too can celebrate it — along with the festival of fire that was given to us when Nehemiah rebuilt the temple and altar and offered the first sacrifices.

**19** Here is the story: When our ancestors were being deported to Persia, some of the devoted priests secretly took fire from the altar and hid it deep in the shaft of a dry cistern, concealing it so carefully that no one could find it.

**20** After many years had gone by, when God's time had come, King Artaxerxes sent Nehemiah back to Judah. Nehemiah sent the priests' descendants to search for the hidden fire. They came back empty-handed — all they found was a thick, muddy liquid.

**21** Nehemiah told them to draw it out and bring it to him anyway. Once the sacrificial animals were arranged on the altar, he had the priests sprinkle the wood and the offerings with the strange liquid.

**22** They did it. Time passed. The sun, which had been hidden behind clouds, broke through — and suddenly a great fire erupted on the altar. Everyone who saw it was astonished.

**23** While the sacrifice burned, the priests led the congregation in prayer, with Jonathan leading and all the rest joining in — Nehemiah among them.

**24** This is the prayer they said: "O LORD, LORD God — Creator of all things — you who are awesome and mighty and righteous and merciful, you who alone are King, you who alone are kind,

**25** you who alone are the great Provider, you who alone are just and all-powerful and eternal, you who have always rescued Israel from every disaster, you who chose our ancestors and made them holy:

**26** receive this sacrifice offered by your whole people Israel. Guard what is yours and make it sacred.

**27** Gather back our scattered people. Free those who are still slaves among foreign nations. Look with compassion on those who are shamed and despised. Show the nations that you are our God.

**28** Bring judgment on those who oppress us and treat us with contempt.

**29** Replant your people in your holy place — as Moses promised."

**30** The priests sang the hymns.

**31** When the sacrifice had been fully consumed, Nehemiah ordered the rest of the liquid poured out over some large stones.

**32** As it ran out, a flame shot up — but it was immediately swallowed by the brilliant light blazing back from the altar itself.

**33** The story spread. Word reached the king of Persia that the exact spot where the exiled priests had hidden the sacred fire had now yielded a miraculous liquid — the liquid with which Nehemiah's people had purified the offerings.

**34** The king sent investigators, verified the story, had the site enclosed and declared holy.

**35** He exchanged gifts with those present, giving with great generosity.

**36** Nehemiah and his associates gave this substance the name "Nephthar," meaning "purification." Most people, though, call it simply "naphtha."
